task.goal: Compile a governed SuperVisuals harness for the split-frame 'Conceptual Contrast / Would You Rather' dish family into a structural Builder contract, without generating final media.
task.success_condition: Preserve the header attribution block, headline/question stem, dual bordered contrast panels, per-panel captions, and all wrong-reading locks intact through Builder's structural contract, with no placeholder text and no duplicated panel captions.
task.atomic_boundary: One raw visual specimen set for one dish variant (statement-contrast or would-you-rather) becomes one structural Builder contract. This harness does not itself render pixels or select final imagery.

source_expression_moment.description: The single claim or binary choice this frame will express — a quote thesis for Conceptual Contrast, or two named alternatives for a Would-You-Rather stem.

voice_context.description: Tone/persona context for how the headline and captions should read in the creator's voice.

dish_variant.description: Which of the two proven dish variants this frame instantiates.

panel_captions.description: The two per-panel captions. Must be distinct strings — identical captions collapse the format's binary premise (see wrong_reading_locks).

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The viewer feels pressure to publicly declare which side of the contrast they identify with, even when the offered opposition is trivial, false, or the two sides were never actually made distinct.
activative_input.stance: Provocative and binary — presents two poles as though only one can be true, then invites public, low-cost commitment to one.
stakes: being seen holding a self-contradictory or 'both sides are the same' position
misreading the two contrasted panels as depicting the same underlying condition
identity_urges: signal which archetype or values I hold by which panel I pick
avoid the expected answer to seem original
activative_input.participation_design: Comment or reply naming which of the two panels represents the viewer's pick, prompted by the bold headline claim or the WOULD YOU RATHER stem; share to tag someone who'd pick the other side.
activative_input.intended_reaction: Viewer picks a side in the comments, converting a single static frame into a debate thread.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: State, in one line, which of the two contrasted panels the viewer identifies with and why.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not let the two panel captions resolve to the same or a non-contrasting string — the format's entire premise is a binary choice, and identical captions on both sides (as shipped in the raw WOULD YOU RATHER specimen) erase the choice entirely.

Do not let unfilled placeholder text (e.g. 'Add a heading') reach final render — placeholder tokens are required-content slots, not decorative defaults, and shipping one is a broken-format failure, not a valid minimal state.
Do not resolve the two image panels to the same or a near-duplicate subject/image — the contrast collapses into a meaningless split-gallery if both slots depict the same person, object, or scene.

Do not let both panel borders render in the same color, or drop the color differentiation entirely in a variant that relies on it — the border color is the format's primary 'these are two distinct poles' signal, not a palette choice.

Do not let the header attribution block (avatar, name, handle) be read as authoring a personal before/after story out of the two contrasted images when the source imagery is stock or third-party — the format asserts an abstract claim or question, not a testimonial, unless the operator explicitly supplies personal-narrative source material.
wrong_reading_locks_meaning: Do not soften the contrast boundary -- PRM-BUS-001 enforces clear perceptual polarization.
Do not distract from core thesis with secondary elements -- PRM-PSY-018 maintains singular focus.
